Courtesy of GKIDS Films Godzilla Minus Zero has scored the biggest opening for a foreign-language live-action film in North America. The Japanese-produced film topped domestic box office charts over the weekend with $31.6 million from 3,254 theaters. The movie is the sequel to Godzilla Minus One , which follows Godzilla’s rampage through post-World War II Japan. The sequel, produced by Toho and directed by Takashi Yamazaki, has a 90 percent audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. “We’re so happy to see audiences embrace ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ at an unprecedented scale for an international film,” says Chance Huskey, VP of distribution for Gkids, the movie’s U.S. distributor. “This landmark release is the result of a thoughtful campaign by Gkids and Toho that emphasized the ‘must see’ intensity of the theatrical experience.” Warner Bros.’s The Cat in the Hat wasn’t as successful. item.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
item.description:
A Kenyan doomsday cult leader was sentenced Friday to 200 years in prison for the murders of 191 people after ordering followers to starve themselves to meet Jesus. Pastor Paul Mackenzie was sentenced by Kenya’s High Court in the coastal city of Mombasa after being convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult, according to the Associated Press. He received two consecutive 100-year terms: one for murders by starvation and another for murders by direct homicide. Justice Diana Kavedza said Mackenzie, the leader of the Good News International Church, bore the “primary criminal culpability” for leading his followers into an isolated area and directing them to starve themselves to death, the outlet reported. “The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law,” the judge added. item.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
item.description:
Paraguay’s president was removed from office and detained after the country’s largest digital bank melted down, leaving half the populace without access to funds and plunging the country into a political crisis. A youth-friendly banking app, Ueno collapsed amid allegations of insider lending and proximity to the country’s longtime ruling party, which is closely aligned with Washington. The app was credited with expanding access in a region where as many as one in four adults does not have a bank account ; its implosion was a “ kind of tsunami in the end ,” a political scientist said, and puts at stake “the credibility of a country that has spent years trying to establish itself as a stable , reliable destination for international investment,” a regional analyst wrote in Americas Quarterly. — Brendan Ruberry

item.description:

The announcement marks a major retreat for a vehicle Musk once touted as one of Tesla’s most ambitious products. Unveiled in 2019 with a futuristic stainless-steel design, the Cybertruck generated enormous attention but struggled to meet Musk’s lofty sales expectations.
